title: Client Connector log modes as users and the API see them: Verbose, user choice, logMode and logLevel

prose.text: What each of Error, Warn, Info and Debug records, the per-profile override of the global default, and the log file size are in [[zcc.app-profiles.logging]]. {{verbose-android}}

prose.label: Who chooses.
prose.text: {{user-choice}} {{android-verbose-logging}} {{android-verbose-api}} Whether that option is the Verbose mode is open {{gap:verbose-option-vs-mode}}. When a device picks up a changed profile is in [[zcc.app-profiles.propagation]].

prose.label: In the API.
prose.text: {{log-mode-is-console-mode}} {{python-log-mode-codes}} The full coding is not documented, and vendor code disagrees on what -1 means {{gap:log-mode-codes}}; the SDKs' readings are compared in [[zcc.api.web-policy-wire:log-mode-minus-one]]. What `logLevel` changes on the device, and how it differs from `logMode`, is open {{gap:level-vs-mode}}. How the Go SDK writes these fields is in [[zcc.api.web-policy-wire:numbers-on-write]].

prose.label: Default.
prose.text: The value of the tenant's global default log mode is not sourced {{gap:default-mode}}.

android-verbose-logging.statement: The Android app profile's Verbose Logging option lets users enable extra debugging logs.

android-verbose-api.statement: By name, the Android block of the web policy carries Verbose Logging as `androidPolicy.enableVerboseLog`, a string the contract gives no description.
android-verbose-api.conditions: Name correspondence only; no source maps enableVerboseLog to the console option or documents its values.

log-mode-is-console-mode.statement: `logMode` in the API is the console's Log Mode: the API reference describes it as the scope of the logs, the console's own words for that setting. `logLevel`, which the API reference describes as a three-step severity (Low 0, Normal 1, High 2), has no counterpart in the captured console articles; `logFileSize` is the maximum log file size.
log-mode-is-console-mode.conditions: Rests on matching descriptions: the console introduces Log Mode "to specify the scope of the logs" and the API reference describes logMode as "the scope of the logs". No source maps logLevel to a console setting.

python-log-mode-codes.statement: The Python SDK's docstring gives example `log_mode` codes: -1 disabled, 0 info, 3 debug; reading -1 as disabled is that docstring's alone.
python-log-mode-codes.conditions: Reworded (v5 item 8, v2 A16): previously stated the codes as the Python SDK's documentation without noting that other vendor code reads -1 differently; the dispute is in gap log-mode-codes.

quotes: log_mode (int): Log mode (e.g. ``-1`` disabled, ``0`` info, ``3`` debug).

verbose-option-vs-mode.title: Whether Android's Verbose Logging option is the Verbose log mode
verbose-option-vs-mode.detail: The Android app profile's Verbose Logging option lets users enable extra debugging logs, and the logging-controls article describes a Verbose mode that logs when invoked by external events such as a Firebase push notification or Mobile Manager flags. No source says the option turns on that mode. Unverified legacy statement: androidPolicy.enableVerboseLog turns on the Firebase-triggered Verbose mode.

log-mode-codes.title: Full integer coding of logMode
log-mode-codes.detail: The API types logMode as an integer (a string on /web/policy/edit) without listing its values. Debug = 3 is corroborated: the Python docstring's example and the Go SDK's UI-captured defaults, whose Log Mode picker is Debug with value 3. What -1 means is disputed: the Python docstring says disabled, the ZCC Terraform provider's schema says -1 disables, and the Go SDK's defaults say -1 means "follow picker". The console UI also sends `logModeSelected` (a label and value) beside `logMode`. The Python SDK's recorded traffic (one test tenant, recorded with SDK 1.9.13, Python SDK cassette) writes logMode -1 with logModeSelected Debug/3 and reads the profile back with logMode -1. Error, Warn and Default remain unknown. Corrects the legacy statement that logMode accepts the strings Error, Warn, Info and Debug, and its SDK example `log_mode="Debug"`.

default-mode.title: The tenant's global default log mode
default-mode.detail: Profiles left on Default follow the global log mode in Platform Settings, whose value is tenant data; the vendor's initial value is not documented. Unverified legacy statements: "Info: Default in most deployments" and "Error: Production default (quiet)". Former zcc-56 asked what log mode a newly created app profile starts with; the profile follows this global value unless overridden (zcc.app-profiles.logging:default-follows-global), so the open question is the global value itself.

level-vs-mode.title: How logLevel differs from logMode
level-vs-mode.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "log_mode — Log mode (may overlap with log_level — exact distinction not documented)." Both keys are in the edit body; the help describes one Log Mode setting. The API reference describes logMode as the scope of the logs and logLevel as a three-step severity (log-mode-is-console-mode), but no source says what logLevel changes on the device.
